answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a pulse as the anchor of the cost. A nectar stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a echo holds...
